subject: chatgptpluginsdirectory.com + PickAPlugin
text:
Hi there,

I came across chatgptpluginsdirectory.com while looking for places that still track the shared ChatGPT and Codex plugin catalog. The task-based browsing is useful, and I liked that you check a public ChatGPT listing before you add anything.

I run PickAPlugin, a smaller hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins (and MCP servers that ship as plugins). Would you be open to a simple link swap? Happy to point people your way from our directories page.

We also published open data on 339 Codex plugin repos (licenses, stars, plugin.json health) that's free to cite: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: A data source for your Codex plugins roundup
text:
Hi Atlas Cloud team,

I read your "10 Best Codex Plugins in 2026" post and liked how you compared bundled skills and MCP servers side by side. That table is clearer than most roundups.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. We pulled GitHub data on 339 open-source plugin repos (median stars, license gaps, how many READMEs mention an API key) and published it here: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

It's CC BY and free to cite if you ever refresh that post. No ask beyond that.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: PickAPlugin for the Awesome Codex Skills resources?
text:
Hi Composio team,

Awesome Codex Skills is one of the lists I keep open when I'm checking new skill packs. The install-from-GitHub path is especially handy.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins and skills. Would you be open to adding it under Resources, or linking our open Codex plugin census? https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

subject: Codex plugin data that might fit Glama
text:
Hi Frank,

Glama is the MCP registry I send people to when they want inspector and gateway tools in the same place. The scale you're at (servers plus live tool calls) is hard to miss.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. A lot of those plugins bundle MCP servers, so we ended up with some cross-over data: of 339 open-source plugin repos, about 18% wire up a remote HTTP/SSE MCP server, and 43% mention an API key in the README.

Full write-up and CSV (CC BY): https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

If it's useful next to one of your MCP posts, a credit link would be great. Happy to link Glama from our side too.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: PickAPlugin for ManyCP's directory list?

subject: Data tip for your Codex + ChatGPT MCP post
text:
Hi Manufact team,

I read your post on OpenAI merging Codex and ChatGPT and what that means for MCP. The shared plugin directory angle is the part most people are still catching up on.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of those plugins. We looked at 339 open-source Codex plugin repos and found 62% also ship a Claude Code manifest, so the cross-host format is already the default for a lot of makers.

Write-up and CSV (CC BY): https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Feel free to cite it if you refresh that post. Thanks either way.

Aaron, PickAPlugin
